summaries.demographer: Kailea Rubel is a 49-year-old non-Hispanic white woman living in Moss Point, Mississippi, where she was raised in a Gulf Coast Baptist family and continues to live with her husband, Tommy (Q84, Q88-Q89, Q97). She completed eleventh grade without a diploma and is now enrolled in GED preparation, marking a later-life educational transition (Q90-Q92). Her household consists of two adults, with adult children and a young grandson nearby rather than co-resident (Q05, Q11, Q51-Q52). She is outside the formal workforce but performs substantial unpaid community and church labor, with occasional informal baking income (Q16, Q65, Q72).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Kailea displays strong budgeting discipline and loss aversion shaped by modest income, storm exposure, medical costs, and household repair risk (Q56-Q64, Q82-Q83). She uses cash envelopes, a paper planner, pantry meals, and delayed purchases to manage scarcity and uncertainty (Q57, Q60-Q61, Q64). Her future-oriented investments are practical and incremental: GED preparation, bakery supplies, and possible certification rather than high-risk ventures (Q18, Q62, Q108). Social incentives matter: church obligations, family expectations, and being useful motivate much of her time allocation (Q16, Q47, Q109).
summaries.political_scientist: Kailea is a Republican-leaning, conservative but not strongly partisan voter who participates in presidential and most local elections (Q23, Q95-Q96). Her political reasoning is locally grounded, emphasizing drainage, schools, disaster response, public safety, health access, and careful spending (Q23-Q25). She has mixed institutional trust: she values police and public services but recognizes unequal treatment and supports practical accountability (Q20-Q30). Her civic identity is strongest through church, volunteering, and community preparedness rather than formal partisan activism (Q16, Q20, Q23, Q47).
summaries.psychologist: Kailea presents as conscientious, relational, practical, and service-oriented, with a self-concept built around reliability, hospitality, faith, and organization (Q01, Q65, Q109). She copes with stress through planning, prayer, walking, baking, choir, and trusted friends, while acknowledging worry about money, storms, caregiving, and education (Q43-Q45, Q50). She is assertive but compassionate in group settings and derives purpose from coordinating others during events and crises (Q02, Q07, Q65). Her motivational architecture combines duty to family, identity as a helper, and a late-life desire to complete unfinished educational and career goals (Q18, Q83, Q108).
